inputs.share_count_basis: 3,847.792m: 4,000m issued less ~152m held by the 2022 Share Award Scheme trustee (no awards ever granted). H1 FY2026 interim note 10 uses 3,847.792m for basic AND diluted EPS ('no dilutive potential shares'). Post-2024 1:4 subdivision basis. Held flat: SBC-zero issuer, no buybacks since 2023.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment expense: 2022 Share Award Scheme has granted no awards since adoption (FY2025 AR Report of the Directors: 239.5m shares available at start and end of year); Share Option Scheme likewise has no grants. SBC-zero market treatment.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases FY2024-H1 FY2026. FY2022 RMB49.9m and FY2023 RMB44.6m were trustee purchases for the share award scheme (the ~152m shares now excluded from the count).
inputs.fx_note: Statements 'Expressed in Renminbi'; HKEX quote in HKD. fx_rate = HKD per CNY 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-16). Parity check against the USD crosses: HKD=X 7.8479 / CNY=X 6.6768 = 1.1754, a 0.3% tie, confirming direction (model CNY x 1.1724 = quote HKD). No dual listing to parity-check. refresh_price.py does not update this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: CNY-built WACC because the flows are RMB. Cost of equity ~9.8%: China 10y CGB ~1.9% + beta ~0.9 x ERP 6.5% + ~2pp size/illiquidity premium for a ~HK$2bn single-asset local railway. After-tax cost of debt ~3.4% (bank loans 3.65-5.5% x (1-25%)). Market-value weights ~79% equity / 21% debt (RMB508m debt vs ~RMB1.77bn market cap). WACC 8.5%, held identical across scenarios: coal-volume and customer-concentration risk is carried in the bear path and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material. Right-of-use assets (RMB210.7m) are prepaid PRC land-use rights paid upfront; there are no lease liabilities on the balance sheet and no lease principal/interest in financing cash flows (FY2025). Land-use-right purchases sit inside 'purchase of PP&E and right-of-use assets', i.e. in capex. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI of RMB27.2m (30 Jun 2026, book) deducted once in the equity bridge. The NCI subsidiary is loss-making (NCI share of FY2025 loss RMB0.36m), so no attributable-flow leakage is applied.
inputs.non_operating_treatment: EBITDA margin path is OPERATING EBITDA, i.e. metrics EBITDA less 'other income, net' (FY2025 30.4m of which FVTPL fair-value gains 33.7m; FY2024 40.9m incl. 19.5m FVTPL gains, 11.7m coal-trading margin, 5.7m consultancy). Operating EBITDA margin: FY2023 40.5%, FY2024 39.0%, FY2025 38.8%, H1 FY2025 45.9%, H1 FY2026 47.5% (H2 is seasonally weaker: H2 FY2025 ~32.5%). Because the FVTPL income is stripped, the matching FVTPL assets (RMB72.2m unlisted HK fund + PRC private-entity stake) and the associate (RMB6.0m) are added in the equity bridge at book.
inputs.capex_note: Capex path is NET of asset-related government grants (FY2025 RMB33.2m and H1 FY2026 RMB13.4m received against the branch-line/upgrade programme). FY2025 gross capex 133.2m (48% of revenue) and H1 FY2026 39.6m reflect the Bohai New Area branch line (roadbed completed 2025) and the Canggang line safety/capacity upgrade; remaining PP&E commitments RMB65.7m at 30 Jun 2026. Steady state ~13.5% of revenue vs D&A ~12%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations. Canggang Railway is a single local freight railway in Hebei (Canggang Line feeding Port Huanghua; coal ~35%+ of tonnage, plus semi-coke, ore fines, coke, oil products) earning tariff-based freight revenue plus loading/unloading and construction/maintenance ancillary services. It is an operating company that owns its line outright (no concession expiry or regulated-asset-base return mechanism found in the filings), so routing is the 'operating company, non-US/cyclical' row, not an infrastructure-concession or RAB model. SBC-zero: house and street bases coincide, band_position null. No final dividend was proposed for FY2025 (FY2024: RMB0.6 cent) and no interim dividend for H1 FY2026. FY0 is FY2025; Y1 = FY2026 is anchored to H1 FY2026 (revenue +23.8%, cargo 8.3mt +23.9%, of which RMB22.6m was one-off special-line construction revenue). Base-year FCF is not a single year: reported FCF was 141.8/74.9/43.1/-2.5/48.2/-49.1 for FY2020-25 because of the capex programme, so the forward FCF is built from components rather than from last_fcf. Price check: at HK$0.54 the market cap is ~RMB1.77bn, ~28x TTM attributable profit (RMB63.1m) and ~16x EV/operating EBITDA - a rich multiple for a coal-weighted single-line railway, which is why every scenario values the stock below the price.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+1.9-2.4%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (-5.1 to -5.9%) and EPS (-1.9 to -5.3%) CAGRs. Revenue fell from RMB376.9m (FY2019) to 258.9m (FY2024) on lower construction/ancillary revenue and coal volumes before recovering to 278.2m (FY2025) and +23.8% in H1 FY2026. EPS CAGRs computed on attributable net income (the eps column is rounded to 0.001 RMB).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (SBC zero; net-debt company so interest income not stripped). FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: FY2025 owner FCF is negative (-49.1m) and FY2023 was -2.5m, both because of the branch-line/upgrade capex programme, not operating losses.

base.narrative: FY2026 +15% on the H1 volume recovery (H2 grows ~10% on a seasonally weaker base), flat FY2027 as the one-off special-line construction revenue drops out, then low-single-digit growth as the Bohai New Area branch line adds industrial-park volume against a slowly plateauing coal flow. Operating EBITDA margin 42-43%, between the FY2023-25 ~39% and the H1 ~46-47%. Capex normalises from the branch-line peak to ~13.5% of revenue by FY2030.

bull.narrative: The western-market sales push (Shanxi, Shaanxi, Inner Mongolia, Ningxia, Xinjiang, Gansu) keeps winning coal, coke and ore-fines flows onto the Canggang Line-Port Huanghua corridor, Hebei's rail-water intermodal policy shifts freight from road to rail, and the branch line ramps quickly. Operating leverage on a largely fixed-cost line lifts operating EBITDA margin to the high-40s (H1 FY2026's 47.5% becomes the full-year norm) and capex falls back toward maintenance once the upgrade programme ends.

bear.narrative: The H1 FY2026 volume rebound proves cyclical: China's thermal-coal flows plateau and decline with the energy transition, oil-product volumes keep falling (-46% in FY2025), and the five largest customers (65% of FY2025 revenue, largest 32.4%) renegotiate or reroute. Revenue reverts toward the FY2024-25 RMB260-280m band, operating EBITDA margin settles at the FY2024-25 H2 run-rate mid-to-high 30s, the branch line under-delivers, and capex stays elevated for safety upgrades. Zero terminal growth on a single coal-weighted line.

scenario_narratives.base: Volume recovery holds but does not compound: FY2026 +15% on H1's 23.9% tonnage rebound, a flat FY2027 as one-off construction revenue rolls off, then 2-4% growth from the Bohai New Area branch line and corridor marketing against plateauing coal. Operating EBITDA margin 42-43%; capex normalises from the branch-line peak to ~13.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Canggang Line-Port Huanghua corridor wins share of western coal, coke and ore-fines flows, Hebei road-to-rail intermodal policy adds tonnage, and the branch line ramps fast. Fixed-cost operating leverage takes operating EBITDA margin to ~48% and capex falls toward maintenance.
scenario_narratives.bear: The rebound is cyclical: thermal-coal volumes peak and fall with China's energy transition, oil products keep shrinking, and a concentrated customer base (top five 65% of revenue) reprices or reroutes. Revenue drifts back to the FY2024-25 band with mid-30s operating margins and elevated safety capex; zero terminal growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: a single railway line, coal-weighted tonnage exposed to China's energy transition, and heavy customer concentration (largest customer 32.4%, top five 65.0% of FY2025 revenue). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once - sustained western-market wins, a fast branch-line ramp and full-year margins at the H1 peak. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the line on what it earns from freight, not on the non-operating income that has propped up reported profit (FVTPL fair-value gains of RMB33.7m were ~45% of FY2025 profit before tax). Operating cash generation is steady at ~RMB100-140m EBITDA, but the line is mid-way through a capex programme and the market already prices it at ~28x earnings, so the DCF asks whether the volume rebound can be capitalised at that multiple - it cannot under any of the three scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: Coal dependence: thermal and coking coal are the core flows; China's coal peak is a structural headwind to terminal growth.
Customer concentration: largest customer 32.4%, top five 65.0% of FY2025 revenue; 77% of trade receivables from the top five.
Capex overrun on the Bohai New Area branch line and Canggang line upgrade (FY2025 capex 48% of revenue) without matching volume.
Non-operating income volatility: FVTPL gains (RMB33.7m FY2025) and coal-trading results swing reported profit; excluded from the operating build and the assets added at book.
Thin liquidity and a HK$0.45-0.94 52-week range: the price can sit far from fundamental value for long periods.
FX: RMB flows against an HKD quote; the HKD per CNY rate is not auto-refreshed.
